scope: Theorem 1.1 of the manuscript “Finite congruence lattices: characterization and undecidability” (preprints/Finite-Congruence-Lattices-Characterization-and-Undecidability-September-24-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 206 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 d26d6cd6285de4f2), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 4. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: The following statements hold. (i) A finite nonempty lattice is representable if and only if it satisfies the finite colored-graph criterion in Theorem 2.2. For each candidate graph size the criterion is decidable by a finite test. (ii) There is no deterministic Turing machine that, given the order table of a finite nonempty lattice, always halts and decides R(L). (iii) There is a nonrepresentable finite lattice L0 of minimum cardinality, specified by the finite formulas in Section 17. Every finite lattice of smaller cardinality is representable, and |L0| > 7. (iv) Given the order table of a finite nonempty lattice L, it is undecidable whether L ∼ = [H, G] for some finite group G and subgroup H ≤ G, where [H, G] is the full subgroup interval.
